title: Public SDK API Design and Behavioral Contracts Check

questions.prompt: Which approach best applies public sdk api design and behavioral contracts?
options: Minimise the public surface and explicitly contract behavior, ownership, failure, threading, lifecycle, and evolution.
questions.answer: Minimise the public surface and explicitly contract behavior, ownership, failure, threading, lifecycle, and evolution.
questions.explanation: The correct response preserves authority, compatibility, exact artifact evidence, adverse-path behavior, and operational ownership.

questions.prompt: If existing consumer source still compiles after rebuilding, the new SDK is necessarily binary-compatible.
questions.explanation: Publishing a Kotlin data class as the request type makes generated constructor, copy, componentN, equality, and property signatures part of evolution risk.

questions.prompt: Why is behavioral compatibility distinct from binary compatibility?
questions.answer: Code can still link while its ordering, errors, side effects, timing, or lifecycle meaning changes and breaks consumers.
questions.explanation: The answer identifies the contract or mechanism that remains valid beyond one implementation demonstration.
